1	# Scientific Background
2	
3	SELFIES is a molecular string representation designed so that generated strings
4	decode to syntactically and semantically valid molecular graphs. The primary
5	paper is:
6	
7	Krenn, Haese, Nigam, Friederich, and Aspuru-Guzik, "SELFIES: a robust
8	representation of semantically constrained graphs with an example application
9	in chemistry", Machine Learning: Science and Technology 1, 045024 (2020), DOI
10	`10.1088/2632-2153/aba947`.
11	
12	The project documentation describes two core translations:
13	
14	- `selfies.encoder(smiles)` translates a SMILES string to SELFIES.
15	- `selfies.decoder(selfies)` translates SELFIES back to SMILES.
16	
17	The encoder preserves the atom order of the input SMILES string. SELFIES
18	strings are interpreted under semantic constraints, which assign bonding
19	capacities to atoms and charged atoms. Under the default constraints, common
20	organic atoms such as carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, sulfur, halogens, and their
21	supported charged forms have finite bonding capacities. If a molecule violates
22	the active constraints and strict encoding is enabled, the encoder reports an
23	error rather than producing a SELFIES string that cannot faithfully represent
24	the molecule.
25	
26	Some SMILES notations use compact forms for delocalized bonding and atom
27	labels. SELFIES itself emits molecular strings under concrete semantic bonding
28	constraints, so the encoder must normalize supported SMILES inputs into an
29	internal molecular graph before the molecule is emitted as SELFIES. For valid
30	inputs, this conversion must preserve atom identities, connectivity, and
31	semantic bonding limits so that the decoded SMILES still represents the same
32	molecular graph.
33	
34	Do not compare molecular strings by plain string equality when a workflow only
35	requires molecular equivalence: different concrete SMILES strings can describe
36	the same graph. For this task, the public reproduction only checks that a
37	documented translation workflow completes for a deterministic catalogue. A
38	correct repair should preserve molecular meaning beyond the supplied catalogue.

118	def _should_invert_chirality(mol, atom):
119	    out_bonds = mol.get_out_dirbonds(atom.index)
120	
121	    # 1. rings whose right number are bonded to this atom (e.g. ...1...X1)
122	    # 2. rings whose left number are bonded to this atom (e.g. X1...1...)
123	    # 3. branches and other (e.g. X(...)...)
124	    partition = [[], [], []]
125	    for i, bond in enumerate(out_bonds):
126	        if not bond.ring_bond:
127	            partition[2].append(i)
128	        elif bond.src < bond.dst:
129	            partition[1].append(i)
130	        else:
131	            partition[0].append(i)
132	    partition[1].sort(key=lambda x: out_bonds[x].dst)
133	
134	    # construct permutation
135	    perm = partition[0] + partition[1] + partition[2]
136	    count = 0
137	    for i in range(len(perm)):
138	        for j in range(i + 1, len(perm)):
139	            if perm[i] > perm[j]:
140	                count += 1
141	    return count % 2 != 0  # if odd permutation, should invert chirality

144	def _fragment_to_selfies(mol, bond_into_root, root,
145	                         attribution_maps, attribution_index=0):
146	    derived = []
147	
148	    bond_into_curr, curr = bond_into_root, root
149	    while True:
150	        curr_atom = mol.get_atom(curr)
151	        token = _atom_to_selfies(bond_into_curr, curr_atom)
152	        derived.append(token)
153	
154	        attribution_maps.append(AttributionMap(
155	            len(derived) - 1 + attribution_index,
156	            token, mol.get_attribution(curr_atom)))
157	
158	        out_bonds = mol.get_out_dirbonds(curr)
159	        for i, bond in enumerate(out_bonds):
160	
161	            if bond.ring_bond:
162	                if bond.src < bond.dst:
163	                    continue
164	
165	                rev_bond = mol.get_dirbond(src=bond.dst, dst=bond.src)
166	                ring_len = bond.src - bond.dst
167	                Q_as_symbols = get_selfies_from_index(ring_len - 1)
168	                ring_symbol = "[{}Ring{}]".format(
169	                    _ring_bonds_to_selfies(rev_bond, bond),
170	                    len(Q_as_symbols)
171	                )
172	
173	                derived.append(ring_symbol)
174	                attribution_maps.append(AttributionMap(
175	                    len(derived) - 1 + attribution_index,
176	                    ring_symbol, mol.get_attribution(bond)))
177	                for symbol in Q_as_symbols:
178	                    derived.append(symbol)
179	                    attribution_maps.append(AttributionMap(
180	                        len(derived) - 1 + attribution_index,
181	                        symbol, mol.get_attribution(bond)))
182	
183	            elif i == len(out_bonds) - 1:
184	                bond_into_curr, curr = bond, bond.dst
185	
186	            else:
187	                # start, end are so we can go back and
188	                # correct offset from branch symbol in
189	                # branch tokens
190	                start = len(attribution_maps)
191	                branch = _fragment_to_selfies(
192	                    mol, bond, bond.dst, attribution_maps, len(derived))
193	                Q_as_symbols = get_selfies_from_index(len(branch) - 1)
194	                branch_symbol = "[{}Branch{}]".format(
195	                    _bond_to_selfies(bond, show_stereo=False),
196	                    len(Q_as_symbols)
197	                )
198	                end = len(attribution_maps)
199	
200	                derived.append(branch_symbol)
201	                for symbol in Q_as_symbols:
202	                    derived.append(symbol)
203	                    attribution_maps.append(AttributionMap(
204	                        len(derived) - 1 + attribution_index,
205	                        symbol, mol.get_attribution(bond)))
206	
207	                # account for branch symbol because it is inserted after
208	                for j in range(start, end):
209	                    attribution_maps[j].index += len(Q_as_symbols) + 1
210	                attribution_maps.append(AttributionMap(
211	                    len(derived) - 1 + attribution_index,
212	                    branch_symbol, mol.get_attribution(bond)))
213	
214	                derived.extend(branch)
215	
216	        # end of chain
217	        if (not out_bonds) or out_bonds[-1].ring_bond:
218	            break
219	    return derived

60	def tokenize_smiles(smiles: str) -> Iterator[SMILESToken]:
61	    """Splits a SMILES string into its tokens.
62	
63	    :param smiles: the input SMILES string.
64	    :return: the tokens of the input SMILES one-by-one with order preserved.
65	    """
66	
67	    i = 0
68	    while i < len(smiles):
69	
70	        if smiles[i] == ".":
71	            yield SMILESToken(None, i, i + 1, SMILESTokenTypes.DOT, smiles[i])
72	            i += 1
73	            continue
74	
75	        if smiles[i] in SMILES_BOND_ORDERS:
76	            bond_idx = i
77	            i += 1
78	        else:
79	            bond_idx = None
80	
81	        if i == len(smiles):
82	            raise SMILESParserError(smiles, "hanging bond", i - 1)
83	
84	        elif smiles[i].isalpha():  # organic subset elements
85	            if smiles[i: i + 2] in ("Br", "Cl"):  # two-letter elements
86	                token = SMILESToken(bond_idx, i, i + 2,
87	                                    SMILESTokenTypes.ATOM, smiles[i: i + 2])
88	            else:  # one-letter elements (e.g. C, N, ...)
89	                token = SMILESToken(bond_idx, i, i + 1,
90	                                    SMILESTokenTypes.ATOM, smiles[i:i + 1])
91	
92	        elif smiles[i] == "[":  # atoms encased in brackets (e.g. [NH])
93	            r_idx = smiles.find("]", i + 1)
94	            if r_idx == -1:
95	                raise SMILESParserError(smiles, "hanging bracket [", i)
96	            token = SMILESToken(bond_idx, i, r_idx + 1,
97	                                SMILESTokenTypes.ATOM, smiles[i:r_idx + 1])
98	
99	        elif smiles[i] in ("(", ")"):  # open and closed branch brackets
100	            if bond_idx is not None:
101	                raise SMILESParserError(smiles, "hanging_bond", bond_idx)
102	            token = SMILESToken(
103	                None, i, i + 1, SMILESTokenTypes.BRANCH, smiles[i:i+1])
104	
105	        elif smiles[i].isdigit():  # one-digit ring number
106	            token = SMILESToken(bond_idx, i, i + 1,
107	                                SMILESTokenTypes.RING, smiles[i:i+1])
108	
109	        elif smiles[i] == "%":  # two-digit ring number (e.g. %12)
110	            rnum = smiles[i + 1: i + 3]
111	            if not (rnum.isnumeric() and len(rnum) == 2):
112	                err_msg = "invalid ring number '%{}'".format(rnum)
113	                raise SMILESParserError(smiles, err_msg, i)
114	            token = SMILESToken(bond_idx, i, i + 3,
115	                                SMILESTokenTypes.RING, smiles[i:i+3])
116	
117	        else:
118	            err_msg = "unrecognized symbol '{}'".format(smiles[i])
119	            raise SMILESParserError(smiles, err_msg, i)
120	
121	        yield token
122	        i = token.end_idx

130	def smiles_to_atom(atom_symbol: str) -> Optional[Atom]:
131	    """Reads an atom from its SMILES representation.
132	
133	    :param atom_symbol: a SMILES atom symbol.
134	    :return: the atom that the input symbol represents.
135	    """
136	
137	    if atom_symbol[0] == "[" and atom_symbol[-1] == "]":
138	        pass  # continue below
139	    elif atom_symbol in ORGANIC_SUBSET:  # e.g. C, N, O, ...
140	        return Atom(atom_symbol, False)
141	    elif atom_symbol in AROMATIC_SUBSET:  # e.g. c, n, o, ...
142	        return Atom(atom_symbol.capitalize(), True)
143	    else:
144	        return None
145	
146	    # e.g. [C], [C@@H], [O-], ...
147	    m = SMILES_BRACKETED_ATOM_PATTERN.match(atom_symbol)
148	    if m is None:
149	        return None
150	    isotope, element, chirality, h_count, charge, _ = m.groups()
151	
152	    isotope = None if (isotope == "") else int(isotope)
153	    is_aromatic = element.islower() and (element in AROMATIC_SUBSET)
154	    element = element.capitalize()
155	    if element not in ELEMENTS:
156	        return None
157	    chirality = None if (chirality == "") else chirality
158	
159	    s = h_count
160	    if s == "":
161	        h_count = 0
162	    else:
163	        s = s[1:]  # HXXX -> XXX
164	        h_count = 1 if (s == "") else int(s)
165	
166	    s = charge
167	    if s == "":
168	        charge = 0
169	    else:
170	        if s[-1].isdigit():  # (+/-)XXX
171	            charge = int(s[1:])
172	        else:  # +++... or ---....
173	            charge = len(s)
174	        charge *= 1 if s[0] == "+" else -1
175	
176	    return Atom(
177	        element=element,
178	        is_aromatic=is_aromatic,
179	        isotope=isotope,
180	        chirality=chirality,
181	        h_count=h_count,
182	        charge=charge
183	    )

221	def _derive_mol_from_tokens(mol, smiles, tokens, i):
222	    tok = None
223	    prev_stack = deque()  # keep track of previous atom on the current chain
224	    branch_stack = deque()  # keep track of open branches
225	    ring_log = dict()  # keep track of hanging ring numbers
226	    chain_start = True
227	
228	    prev_stack.append(tok)
229	    while tokens:
230	        tok = tokens.popleft()
231	        bond_char = tok.extract_bond_char(smiles)
232	        symbol, symbol_type = tok.extract_symbol(smiles), tok.token_type
233	        prev_atom = prev_stack[-1]
234	
235	        if symbol_type == SMILESTokenTypes.DOT:
236	            break
237	
238	        elif symbol_type == SMILESTokenTypes.ATOM:
239	            curr = smiles_to_atom(symbol)
240	            if curr is None:
241	                err_msg = "invalid atom symbol '{}'".format(symbol)

243	
244	            curr, i = _attach_atom(mol, bond_char, curr, prev_atom, i, tok)
245	            prev_stack.pop()
246	            prev_stack.append(curr)
247	            chain_start = False
248	
249	        elif chain_start:
250	            err_msg = "SMILES chain begins with non-atom"
251	            raise SMILESParserError(smiles, err_msg, tok.start_idx)
252	
253	        elif symbol_type == SMILESTokenTypes.BRANCH:
254	            if symbol == "(":
255	                branch_stack.append(tok)
256	                prev_stack.append(prev_atom)
257	                chain_start = True
258	            else:
259	                if not branch_stack:
260	                    err_msg = "hanging ')' bracket"
261	                    raise SMILESParserError(smiles, err_msg, tok.start_idx)
262	                branch_stack.pop()
263	                prev_stack.pop()
264	
265	        elif symbol_type == SMILESTokenTypes.RING:
266	            if symbol not in ring_log:
267	                lpos = mol.add_placeholder_bond(src=prev_atom.index)
268	                ring_log[symbol] = (tok, prev_atom, lpos)
269	            else:
270	                ltoken, latom, lpos = ring_log.pop(symbol)
271	                _make_ring_bonds(
272	                    mol=mol, smiles=smiles,
273	                    ltoken=ltoken, latom=latom, lpos=lpos,
274	                    rtoken=tok, ratom=prev_atom
275	                )
276	
277	        else:
278	            # should not happen
279	            raise Exception("invalid symbol type")
280	        i += 1
281	
282	    if len(mol) == 0:
283	        err_idx = (len(smiles) if (tok is None) else tok.start_idx) - 1
284	        raise SMILESParserError(smiles, "empty SMILES fragment", err_idx)
285	
286	    if branch_stack:

288	        raise SMILESParserError(smiles, "hanging '(' bracket", err_idx)
289	
290	    if ring_log:
291	        rnum, (tok, _, _) = list(ring_log.items())[-1]
292	        err_msg = "hanging ring number '{}'".format(rnum)
293	        raise SMILESParserError(smiles, err_msg, tok.start_idx)

## Root cause

The failure was in aromatic kekulization: `MolecularGraph._prune_from_ds` (`source/selfies/mol_graph.py:301`). Before finding a perfect matching on the delocalization subgraph, atoms that cannot receive a double bond are pruned. For bracketed aromatic atoms (fixed H count) the rule was:

```python
free = (valences[-1] - charge) - used;  prune unless free is odd
```

That parity shortcut decides correctly for odd-parity elements like N (`[n]`, `[nH]`, `[nH+]`), but mis-prunes depleted even-valence atoms with no attached H — concretely `[c]` (2 aromatic bonds, H0 provides 2 slots, parity says prune). In the scaffold's 7-membered ring (`-c3[c]n(Br)ccs[nH]3`), pruning `[c]` left its neighboring aromatic carbon with no possible match partner, so `find_perfect_matching` returned `None` → `EncoderError: kekulization failed`.

## Fix

Replaced the parity formula with the same saturation test the implicit-H branch already uses: a bracketed aromatic atom is prunable only if its used electrons — aromatic bonds counted as single, plus the fixed H count, plus |charge| — exactly fill one of its permitted aromatic valences; otherwise it must receive a double bond. Notably, lone-pair donors still prune (`[nH]`, `[oH+]` used=3 ∈ (3,5)/(2,4)), as do Cp-type anions (`[cH-]` 3+1=4 ∈ (4,)) and tropylium (`[cH+]`), while `[c]`, `[n]`, `[nH+]` now correctly keep and take a double bond.

- Public smoke test: 7/7 pass, exit `0`.

- 16 drug-like molecules (incl. the scaffold) round-trip with exact graph identity — atoms, charges, H counts, isotopes, chirality, and bond orders all preserved.
- Constraint enforcement untouched: `[CH5]`, `O=CO=O`, `N(C)(C)(C)(C)`, `Cl(Cl)(Cl)` etc. still raise `EncoderError` in strict mode; `strict=False`, `attribute=True`, stereochemistry (`@`/`/`/`\`), multi-digit ring numbers, and disconnected fragments all behave as documented.
